newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Forasol set to merge with Pride - AVH.
newsitem.headline: Forasol set to merge with Pride - AVH.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ackermans & van Haaren (AVH) said on Monday its Forasol-Foramer NV unit was due to merge with U.S. Pride Petroleum Services Inc.

AVH said that under the agreement, which was still subject to due diligence and approval of boards and authorities, Forasol shareholders could swap one Forasol share for 0.66 Pride share plus $6.80 in cash.

AVH, whose shares were suspended on the Brussels bourse on Monday pending the statement, said it would obtain about 1.07 billion Belgian francs ($34.1 million) in cash plus a stake of about 7.2 percent in Pride, a Houston-based provider of contract drilling and plugging and abandonment services.
It said it expected to make consolidated capital gain of about 1.0 billion francs on the deal.

AVH said it expected the final closing of the merger in the first quarter of 1997. It said it could still deconsolidate Forasol in 1996 and book the capital gain if the timing of the operation was respected.

AVH has a 30 percent stake in Forasol, an on- and offshore drilling company, listed on U.S. stock market Nasdaq in May. French group Soletanche also has 30 percent. The rest of the Forasol shares is listed.
AVH said the merged group expected to realise turnover of more than $750 million in 1997, of which about 30 percent from offshore operations. ($ = 31.36 Belgian Francs)
Forasol will work as operational division of the Pride group. Its executive management will join the new management committee of Pride, which is expecting turnover of more than $400 million for 1996.

The AVH statement said Pride would enable Forasol to consolidate its land activities in a bigger structure. Forasol gave Pride access to offshore markets in Africa and Asia and specific technological know-how.
